reason: E3 directly supports lattice distortion enhancing strength and corrosion resistance in an amorphous AlTiVNb film, but the cited evidence does not establish that light-element additions cause the lattice distortion, nor that lattice distortion promotes protective oxide formation. E1 and E2 provide only general context on lightweight HEA corrosion and processing, without addressing the specific mechanistic premises.
premises: High fractions of light elements (Al, Ti) in lightweight HEAs generate pronounced lattice distortion
Lattice distortion enhances solid-solution strengthening by reducing dislocation mobility
Lattice distortion promotes formation of a homogeneous, adherent, protective oxide/passive layer at high temperatures
Amorphous or nano-crystalline microstructures can be achieved by controlled processing and contribute to these effects
The combined effects yield low density with high strength and corrosion/oxidation resistance
